🇲🇽🏛️ <u>HOW NEOLIBERALISM ERASED THE SOCIAL ECONOMY FROM MEXICO'S CLASSROOMS</u>

Contralínea rescues Sarah Babb's study of UNAM economics theses: from the 1940s to the 70s the dominant authors were Marx and Keynes; by the "lost decade" of the 80s the syllabus belonged to Hayek and Friedman. Political economy gave way to sterile econometrics — and the social economy of cooperatives and collective enterprise was simply deleted from the curriculum. What neoliberalism expelled from the university is now rebuilding itself in public policy.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MURDERED MORELOS MAYOR WAS HIMSELF UNDER INVESTIGATION FOR CARTEL TIES: HARFUCH</u>

Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch revealed that Valentín Lavín, the Temoac mayor killed inside his own city hall, was being investigated for links to the Los Aparicio / Los Huazulco cell — and for possible intellectual participation in the murders of activists Samir Flores and Sandra Camacho. His mother-in-law "La Patrona," the municipal treasurer, is already detained as an alleged operational leader. In Mexico, investigations don't get buried with the bodies.

🇲🇽📚 <u>"HATE SPEECH IS NOT JUST AN OPINION": MEXICO'S SCIENCE CHIEF TAKES ON THE FAR RIGHT</u>

At a Secihti forum on the far right as a political phenomenon, Secretary Rosaura Ruiz drew the line: when discourse slides into hate, exclusion, racism, misogyny or historical denialism, "hate speech is not simply opinion" — it legitimizes discrimination and opens the door to violence. Her diagnosis, for Mexico and the world: the far right "is no longer marginal; it has begun displacing the traditional right."

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICANS FEEL SAFER THAN AT ANY POINT IN THE SHEINBAUM ERA: INEGI</u>

INEGI's ENSU survey puts urban insecurity perception at 59.8% in June — the lowest reading since Sheinbaum took office, down from 61.7% in December 2024 and 63.2% a year ago. Ciudad Nezahualcóyotl collapsed from 55.5% to 41.3% in a single quarter; Nuevo Laredo is down to 26.5%. Homicides cut in half, and now perception follows. The "failed state" headline writers will ignore this one too.

text: 🇲🇽🪰 In two weeks, Mexico begins releasing sterile flies against the screwworm — north to south. "We've been working on this with all the ranchers' organizations and with governors to contain the screwworm plague. The Chiapas plant is already open, and a new, more efficient strain is now being analyzed." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, in Cuautla, Morelos The sterile insect technique is the proven weapon against the New World screwworm. Mexico built its own production plant in Metapa, Chiapas. Releases start in about two weeks, moving from north to south — paving the way for the full reopening of cattle exports to the US.

🇲🇽🌎 The US is reopening its border to Mexican cattle — after a year of coordinated work. "It's very good news, because all the cattle ranchers in the country — particularly those in the north who raise cattle and then export to the United States — will recover this export. It helps all these families and, in general, the country's economy." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, in Cuautla, Morelos Sheinbaum received a letter Friday from US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins confirming the reopening. The plan: Sonora opens the third week of August, then two crossings in Chihuahua, then a full reopening. The screwworm-related closure hit ranchers on both sides — beef prices in the US rose because of it too. The work was coordinated between Panama, the US, and Mexico.

text:
🇲🇽🌐🔥 Washington wants Mexico to wall off China. Sheinbaum is taking her time.

The US refused to extend the USMCA for another 16 years, triggering annual reviews, and the first joint review opened July 1. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer was in Mexico City on July 23 with a clear demand: stricter rules of origin, higher regional-content thresholds, and screening to keep Chinese inputs out — all framed as stopping "Chinese goods entering through the back door."

Sheinbaum refuses to be rushed. Mexico will not answer Washington's proposed 10% tariff, she said, until it "has presented its arguments through the formal channel." The peso is forecast to slide toward 18 per dollar on the uncertainty — yet Mexico still holds the strongest card at the table: it is the No. 1 trading partner of the United States, with record exports of roughly $50 billion in April alone.

Being Washington's top supplier is leverage, not obedience. Mexico will not sign away its right to diversify — toward China, the EU, the Global South — just to calm US anxieties. In a multipolar world, sovereignty means keeping every door open.

🐉🇲🇽 1 in 6 cars sold in Mexico is now Chinese — and Mexico's own 50% tariff didn't stop it

Chinese brands hit 17% of new-vehicle sales in Mexico in the first half of 2026, up from 14% a year earlier — 137,525 cars, a jump of nearly 30%. In 2020 they were under 1% of the market. This surge happened despite Mexico's own decision to raise light-vehicle tariffs from 20% to 50% in January, aimed squarely at countries without a free-trade deal.

Read it as sovereignty, not surrender. Imports of Chinese cars actually collapsed 82% from their November 2025 peak, and Mexico fell from the world's No. 1 buyer of Chinese vehicles to No. 16. The tariff is Mexico's own industrial policy — protecting local jobs and building leverage for the USMCA review — not an order from Washington. Beijing protested that it hits $30 billion in Chinese exports, $9 billion of it autos.

Mexico taxes China when it serves Mexican industry, and buys from China when it serves Mexican consumers. Automakers are eating the tariff rather than leaving. That is what strategic autonomy looks like: Mexico sets the terms, and everyone still wants in.
